before: AI agents for monitoring and supervising fused filament 3D printing
after: Local language model agents for monitoring and supervising fused filament 3D printing

before: Printer operators need to know what is happening during a print and what action to take. We present a local AI agent system for fused filament fabrication, a form of 3D printing. The system connects written requests to saved measurements and printer services. A supervisor agent sends data questions to a database agent. It sends printer requests to a printing agent. Tools return records or confirm that a request was accepted. Separate camera and contact acoustic emission (AE) services can request a pause without waiting for the AI conversation. The system keeps agents, tools, saved data and computing tasks separate. An AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 computer with 64 GB memory hosts the language model. NVIDIA hardware supports visual-model training. We describe image labeling, model training, data storage and the order of tool calls. We also describe how records can be linked by print job, time and commanded position. Supporting tests compare six visual models and five AE classifiers. Each model is fitted with three random seeds on fixed data splits. YOLO11n detection reaches image macro F1 of 0.940 ± 0.043 and box AP50 of 0.720 ± 0.013. A small AE neural network reaches macro F1 of 0.773 ± 0.000. These scores support model selection. They do not measure agent-task success or combined-sensor performance.
after: Printer operators need to know what is happening during a print and what action to take. We present a local artificial intelligence (AI) agent system for fused filament fabrication, a form of 3D printing. A supervisor sends data questions to a database agent and printer requests to a printing agent. Tools return records or confirm that a request was accepted. Separate camera and contact acoustic emission (AE) services can request a pause without waiting for the AI conversation. The system keeps agents, tools, stored data and computing tasks separate. An AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 computer with 64 GB memory is the designated language-model deployment host. NVIDIA hardware supports visual-model training. We describe labeling, training, storage and tool calls, and an architecture linking records by job, time and commanded position. Supporting tests compare six visual models and five AE classifiers, each fitted with three random seeds on fixed data splits. YOLO11n detection reaches image macro F1 of 0.940 ± 0.043, which combines precision and recall with equal class weighting. Its box average precision at an intersection-over-union threshold of 0.50 (AP50) is 0.720 ± 0.013. A small AE multilayer perceptron reaches macro F1 of 0.773 ± 0.000. These scores support recognition-model selection. They do not measure agent-task success or paired-sensor fusion performance.

before: Fused filament fabrication (FFF) makes a part by placing heated plastic along a planned path. The printer adds one layer at a time. Good printing depends on steady plastic flow, suitable temperature, correct movement and good adhesion. A problem can grow over several layers and waste material before the operator notices it. Monitoring should detect a change, connect it to the current print and help the operator choose a response. Reviews of material-extrusion monitoring discuss these linked tasks (Fu et al. 2021; Oleff et al. 2021; Lu and Wong 2018).
after: Fused filament fabrication (FFF) makes a part by placing heated thermoplastic along a planned path. The printer adds one layer at a time. Good printing depends on steady plastic flow, suitable temperature, correct movement and good adhesion. A problem can grow over several layers and waste material before the operator notices it. Monitoring should detect a change, connect it to the current print and help the operator choose a response. Reviews of material-extrusion monitoring discuss these linked tasks (Fu et al., 2021; Lu & Wong, 2018; Oleff et al., 2021).

before: Large language models (LLMs) let operators ask for records and printer actions in everyday language. Manufacturing systems use specialized agents and tools to connect these requests to process data (Holland and Chaudhari 2024; Lim et al. 2024; Elbasheer et al. 2026). Our agents work alongside the sensor services. A rule based on repeated detections can request a pause without waiting for an LLM answer. This keeps the sensor response separate from the conversation. We can then test each task at the speed it needs.
after: Large language models (LLMs) let operators ask for records and printer actions in everyday language. Manufacturing systems use specialized agents and tools to connect these requests to process data (Elbasheer et al., 2026; Holland & Chaudhari, 2024; Lim et al., 2024). Our agents work alongside the sensor services. A rule based on consecutive detections can request a pause without waiting for an LLM answer. This keeps the sensor response separate from the conversation. We can then evaluate sensing, reasoning and operator interaction separately.

before: The best visual model depends on the output we need. An image classifier gives one label for the whole image. An object detector also draws boxes around possible defects. Boxes help an operator see where to look, but they require more detailed labels for training. A whole-image label may be enough for an alarm. Classification accuracy and box average precision measure different things, so we should not compare them as if they were the same score. We use the same images for both model types. We compare their image decisions and check box quality separately.

Boxes help an operator see where to look, but they require more detailed labels for training. A whole-image label may be enough for an alarm. Classification accuracy and box average precision measure different things, so we should not compare them as if they were the same score. We use the same images for both model types. We compare their image decisions and check box quality separately.

before: AE model choice also depends on accuracy and computing cost. Linear models, groups of decision trees and small neural networks can all use features taken from an acoustic burst. Their decision cutoffs, input scaling and speed affect the monitoring service. A model may rank events well but give weaker normal-or-defective decisions at one cutoff. We therefore check more than overall accuracy. We also check performance across classes, missed defects, false alarms and the quality of probability estimates.
after: AE model choice also depends on accuracy and computing cost. Linear models, groups of decision trees and small neural networks can all use features taken from an acoustic burst. Their decision thresholds, input scaling and speed affect the monitoring service. A decision threshold is the score needed to choose a class. A model may rank events well but give weaker normal-or-defective decisions at one threshold. We therefore check more than overall accuracy. We also check performance across classes, missed defects, false alarms and the quality of probability estimates.

before: We study how an operator's request reaches the right data source or printer service. We also study how the system returns an answer that the operator can check. We describe the supervisor, its specialist agents and the information passed through each tool. We test the visual and acoustic models that provide this information. The agent workflow and the recognition tests belong in the same paper, but they need different measures of success.
after: We study how an operator's request reaches the right data source or printer service. We also study how the system returns an answer that the operator can check. before: Reviews of machine learning in additive manufacturing discuss data quality and deployment as well as model training (Qin et al. 2022; Kumar et al. 2023). Closely related samples or choices based on test results can make a model seem better on new data than it really is (Kapoor and Narayanan 2023). Probability quality is a separate issue. A high model score is not always a reliable chance estimate (Guo et al. 2017). We keep the data splits fixed, choose decision cutoffs using validation data and state what each speed test includes. We describe sensor linking as a system design. Our numerical tests cover the individual recognition models.

before: The Vallen VS600-Z1 is a passive contact AE sensor. Its nominal resonance is near 600 kHz, and its stated frequency band is 550–730 kHz. The spotWave 201 has one data channel, 16-bit conversion and a rated sample rate of 2 MHz (Vallen Systeme n.d.-a, n.d.-b). The fixture carries elastic waves from near the extrusion area to the sensor. This records short, high-frequency waves through solid material. It does not measure airborne sound or the low-frequency vibration measured by an accelerometer. Mounting, contact, gain and filtering affect how the recorded signal relates to the printing process.

before: Two application tools connect the agents to data and printer services. The database tool receives an SQL statement, which is a request for database records. It checks the statement and uses a table library to get SQLite rows. It returns a table, a message that no rows were found, or an error. The interface shows the query and its result. The printer tool receives an operation and any needed filename, target temperature, feed setting or flow setting. It then calls OctoPrint. Table 3 lists these inputs, replies and effects. Camera capture, feature processing and saving records run in the background. They are not conversation tool calls.
after: Two application tools connect the agents to data and printer services. The database tool receives an SQL statement, which is a request for database records. It checks SQL syntax by parsing the statement, then uses a table library to execute the query and return SQLite rows. This syntax check is not an authorization policy. It returns a table, a message that no rows were found, or an error. The interface shows the query and its result. The printer tool receives an operation and any needed filename, target temperature, feed setting or flow setting. It then calls OctoPrint. Table 3 lists these inputs, replies and effects. Camera capture, feature processing and saving records run in the background. They are not conversation tool calls.

before: For AE, sensitivity is the share of defective observations correctly found. Specificity is the share of normal observations correctly rejected as defects. AUROC summarizes how well the scores rank defective and normal observations across cutoffs. The Brier score averages the squared difference between predicted defect probability and the actual binary label. Expected calibration error (ECE) checks how closely predicted probabilities match observed outcomes. We use 15 equal-width probability bins and weight each bin by its observation count (Guo et al. 2017). We report these checks without adding a separate probability-calibration step after fitting.
after: For AE, sensitivity is the share of defective observations correctly found. Specificity is the share of normal observations correctly classified as normal. Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) summarizes how well the scores rank defective and normal observations across decision thresholds. The receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve plots sensitivity against the false-positive rate. The Brier score averages the squared difference between predicted defect probability and the actual binary label. Expected calibration error (ECE) checks how closely predicted probabilities match observed outcomes. We use 15 equal-width probability bins and weight each bin by its observation count (Guo et al., 2017). We report these checks without adding a separate probability-calibration step after fitting.
